cards.grammarNote:
**النَّتيجة** (an-natīja) = the score/result. The definite article **ال** (al-) is attached; before sun letters like ن, the ل assimilates: al- → an-.
**كم** (kam) = 'how much/many' — used to ask a numeric value.

**نُقطة** (nuqṭa) = a point (in scoring). Plural: **نِقاط** (niqāṭ).
**سَجَّلنا** (sajjalnā) = 'we scored'; the verb سَجَّل uses the فَعَّل pattern indicating intensity.

**مُباراة** (mubārāh) = a match or game. From the root ب-ر-ي on مُفاعَلة pattern, implying mutual contest.
Plural: **مُباريات** (mubāriyāt).
cards.englishPhrase: There is a soccer match today.

cards.grammarNote:
**بُطولة** (buṭūla) = tournament, championship. From **بَطَل** (baṭal) 'hero/champion'.
**فازَ بـ** (fāza bi-) = 'to win (something)' — the preposition بـ is required.

**مُنافِس** (munāfis) = opponent, rival. Active participle of نافَسَ 'to compete with'.
**قَوِيّ** (qawiyy) = strong — adjectives agree in gender; fem. **قَوِيَّة**.

**فازَ** (fāza) = he won. Root ف-و-ز. The past tense (ماضي) is used for completed actions.
Future: **سَيَفوز** (sa-yafūz). 'We won': **فُزنا** (fuznā).

**خَسِرَ** (khasira) = he lost (a game). Root خ-س-ر. Opposite of فازَ.
**خَسِرنا** (khasirnā) = we lost; past tense with first-person plural suffix.

**حَكَم** (ḥakam) = referee, umpire. From root ح-ك-م 'to judge/rule'.
**صافَرَ** (ṣāfara) = to blow a whistle — verb on فاعَل pattern.

**مَلعَب** (mal'ab) = stadium, sports ground. Noun of place from ل-ع-ب 'to play'.
**مَمتلِئ** (mumtali') = full/crowded — active participle of امتَلَأَ.
cards.englishPhrase: There are many people in the stadium.

cards.grammarNote:
**مُدَرِّب** (mudarrib) = coach, trainer. Active participle from دَرَّبَ 'to train (someone)'.
Fem.: **مُدَرِّبة** (mudarriba). Definite: **المُدَرِّب** (al-mudarrib).

**بَطَل** (baṭal) = champion, hero. Fem.: **بَطَلة** (baṭala).
**بَطَل العالَم** = world champion — an إضافة (iḍāfa) possessive construct: no ال on the first noun.

**فَريق** (farīq) = team. Plural: **فُرَق** (furaq).
Possession: **فَريقُنا** (farīqunā) = 'our team' — add the suffix ـنا directly.

**لاعِب** (lā'ib) = player. Active participle of لَعِبَ 'to play'. Plural: **لاعِبون** (lā'ibūn).
**أَفضَل** (afḍal) = the best — elative (superlative) adjective.

**تَعادُل** (ta'ādul) = tie/draw. Verbal noun (مصدر) of تَعادَلَ 'to draw'.
**انتَهَت بـ** (intahat bi-) = 'ended in/with' — the preposition بـ follows the verb.
cards.englishPhrase: The game ended in a tie.

cards.grammarNote:
**رياضيّ** (riyāḍiyy) = athlete; adjective-noun from **رياضة** (riyāḍa) 'sport'.
Fem.: **رياضيَّة** (riyāḍiyya). Indefinite: no ال, and the tanwīn ending ـٌ appears in formal Arabic.

**رياضة** (riyāḍa) = sport, athletics. Plural: **رياضات** (riyāḍāt).
**أُحِبّ** (uḥibb) = I like/love — فعل مضارع (present tense) from root ح-ب-ب.

**مُسابَقة** (musābaqa) = competition, contest. From سابَقَ 'to race/compete with'.
**شَديد** (shadīd) = intense — adjective that follows the noun and agrees in gender.

**سَجَّلَ** (sajjala) = to score/record. **هَدَف** (hadaf) = goal; indefinite accusative **هَدَفًا** as the object.
Plural of هَدَف: **أَهداف** (ahdāf).

**بيكلبول** (bīklbūl) = pickleball, a transliterated loanword with no Arabic root.
Loanwords are treated as masculine singular nouns by default in MSA.

**مَضرَب** (maḍrab) = racket/paddle. A noun of instrument/place from ض-ر-ب 'to hit'.
Plural: **مَضارِب** (maḍārib). Adjective **جَديد** (jadīd) = new, follows the noun.

**مَلعَب** (mal'ab) = court/playing field. Noun of place from ل-ع-ب 'to play'.
**فارِغ** (fāriḡ) = empty — adjective agreeing in gender with the noun.

**إِرسال** (irsāl) = a serve (in sports); also 'sending'. Verbal noun of أَرسَلَ 'to send'.
Verb form: **أَرسِل** (arsil) = serve! — imperative.

**تَبادُل ضَربات** (tabādul ḍarabāt) = a rally; lit. 'exchange of strokes'. An إضافة (iḍāfa) construct.
**طَويل** (ṭawīl) = long — adjective agreeing in gender.

**كُرة** (kura) = ball. Fem. noun; plural: **كُرات** (kurāt).
**خارِج الحُدود** (khārij al-ḥudūd) = out of bounds — preposition + إضافة.

**شَبَكة** (shabaka) = net; also 'network'. Fem. noun from ش-ب-ك 'to interweave'.
**ضَرَبَت** (ḍarabat) = hit (fem. subject) — verb agrees in gender with الكُرة (fem.).

**تَنَزُّه** (tanazzuh) = hiking, an outing on foot. Verbal noun of تَنَزَّهَ 'to go for a walk/hike'.
**نَذهَب للتَّنَزُّه** = 'we go hiking' — للـ (li-) before a verbal noun expresses purpose.
cards.englishPhrase: We go hiking on the weekend.
cards.phrase: نَذهَب للتَّنَزُّه في عُطلة نِهاية الأُسبوع.

cards.grammarNote:
**مَسار** (masār) = trail, path, route. Noun of place from س-ي-ر 'to travel'.
**ضَيِّق** (ḍayyiq) = narrow — adjective following the noun, agreeing in gender.

**جَبَل** (jabal) = mountain. Plural: **جِبال** (jibāl) — a broken plural.
**مُرتَفِع** (murtafi') = high/elevated — active participle used as adjective.

**حَقيبة ظَهر** (ḥaqība ẓahr) = backpack; lit. 'back bag' — an إضافة (iḍāfa) construct.
**ثَقيلة** (thaqīla) = heavy — fem. adjective agreeing with حَقيبة (fem.).

**دَرّاجة** (darrāja) = bicycle. Fem. noun; lit. 'rolling thing' from د-ر-ج 'to roll'.
**دَرّاجَتي** (darrājatī) = my bicycle — possessive suffix ـي drops the tā' marbūṭa ة and adds ـتي.

**رَكِبَ** (rakiba) = to ride (a vehicle or animal) — takes a direct object.
**كُلَّ يَوم** (kulla yawm) = every day — كُلّ (kull) + a definite noun in genitive = distributive.
cards.englishPhrase: I ride a bike every day.

cards.grammarNote:
**خَوذة** (khawdha) = helmet. Fem. noun.
**اِرتَدِ** (irtadi) = put on (an item of clothing/gear) — imperative of اِرتَدى.

**سِباق** (sibāq) = race. Verbal noun of سابَقَ 'to race against'.
**فازَ في السِّباق** (fāza fī as-sibāq) = 'won the race' — في marks participation.

**الهَواء الطَّلق** (al-hawā' aṭ-ṭalq) = the open air, outdoors; lit. 'free/open air'.
**أَنشِطة** (anshiṭa) = activities — broken plural of نَشاط (nashāṭ).

**خَطّ النِّهاية** (khaṭṭ an-nihāya) = finish line; an إضافة: 'line of the end'.
**وَصَلَ** (waṣala) = to arrive/reach — takes the preposition إلى.
cards.englishPhrase: He reached the finish line first.

cards.grammarNote:
**تَمرين** (tamrīn) = exercise, training (noun). Verb: **تَمَرَّنَ** (tamarrana) = to exercise.
**كُلَّ صَباح** (kulla ṣabāḥ) = every morning — distributive كُلّ + genitive.

**إِطالة** (iṭāla) = stretching; verbal noun of أَطالَ 'to lengthen'. Also **تَمدُّد** (tamaddud).
**قَبلَ** (qabla) + noun = 'before (something)' — a temporal preposition.

**عَرَق** ('araq) = sweat (noun). Verb: **تَعَرَّقَ** or **عَرِقَ** ('ariqa) = to sweat.
**كَثيرًا** (kathīran) = a lot — adverb in accusative form.

**تَدريب** (tadrīb) = training. Verbal noun of دَرَّبَ 'to train (someone)'.
**شاقّ** (shāqq) = tough, hard — adjective following the noun.

**سُرعة** (sur'a) = speed. Fem. noun from س-ر-ع 'to be fast'.
**سَريع** (sarī') = fast (adj., masc.); **سَريعة** (sarī'a) = fem. — agrees with the noun it describes.

**مُتعَب** (muta'ab) = tired; passive participle of أَتعَبَ 'to tire (someone)'.
**تَعبان** (ta'bān) is a colloquial variant. In a predicate: **أنا مُتعَب** with no verb 'to be' needed in present tense.

**إِصابة** (iṣāba) = injury. Verbal noun of أَصابَ 'to hit/injure'.
**خِلالَ** (khilāla) = during — preposition taking a genitive noun.
cards.englishPhrase: He got injured during the game.

cards.grammarNote:
**ماء** (mā') = water. Masc. noun; one of the classical words with hamza.
**اِشرَب** (ishrab) = drink! — imperative of شَرِبَ. **الكَثير مِن** = 'a lot of'.
cards.englishPhrase: Remember to drink lots of water.
cards.phrase: تَذَكَّر أَن تَشرَب الكَثير مِن الماء.
cards.phraseRomanized: tadhakkar an tashrab al-kathīr min al-mā'.

cards.grammarNote:
**إِحماء** (iḥmā') = warm-up; verbal noun of أَحمى 'to warm'. Also verb **يَتَحَمَّى**.
**لِنَبدَأ** (linabda') = 'let's begin' — jussive with لِـ prefix for first person plural.

**الكود** (al-kōd) = the code — a loanword treated as masc. singular.
MSA alternative: **الشِّفرة** (ash-shifra) or **الكود البَرمَجيّ**.
**نَظيف** (naẓīf) = clean — adjective following a definite noun.

**بَرمَجة** (barmaja) = programming (noun). Verb: **بَرمَجَ** (barmaja) = to program.
Root ب-ر-م-ج is a quadriliteral borrowed from 'program'. **أُحِبّ** (uḥibb) = I like.
cards.englishPhrase: I like to code at night.

cards.grammarNote:
**البَرنامِج** (al-barnāmij) = the program/software. Plural: **البَرامِج** (al-barāmij) — broken plural.
MSA also uses **البَرمَجِيّات** for 'software' as a collective term.
cards.englishPhrase: This software is easy to use.

cards.grammarNote:
**مُهَندِس** (muhandis) = engineer. Fem.: **مُهَندِسة** (muhandisa).
**مُهَندِس بَرمَجِيّات** = software engineer — an إضافة (iḍāfa): no ال on the first noun.

**مُطَوِّر** (muṭawwir) = developer. Active participle of طَوَّرَ 'to develop'.
**واجِهة أمامِيّة** (wājihat amāmiyya) = front-end — fem. iḍāfa phrase.

**الحاسوب** (al-ḥāsūb) = the computer. From ح-س-ب 'to compute'. Colloquial: **الكمبيوتر**.
**سَريع** (sarī') = fast — adjective agreeing in gender (masc. here).

**حاسوب مَحمول** (ḥāsūb maḥmūl) = laptop; lit. 'portable computer'. **مَحمول** = passive participle of حَمَلَ 'to carry'.
Also loanword **لابتوب** in colloquial use.

**لَوحة المَفاتيح** (lawḥat al-mafātīḥ) = keyboard; lit. 'board of keys'. An iḍāfa.
**مَفاتيح** = broken plural of **مِفتاح** (miftāḥ) 'key'.
cards.englishPhrase: This keyboard is nice to use.

cards.grammarNote:
**الشَّاشة** (ash-shāsha) = the screen, monitor. Fem. noun; ش is a sun letter so ال assimilates.
**ساطِع** (sāṭi') = bright — adjective agreeing in gender (masc.).

**خَطَأ بَرمَجيّ** (khaṭa' barmajiyy) = a programming bug/error. Also the loanword **بَاگ** in informal use.
**في** (fī) = in — takes a genitive noun.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a bug in the code.

cards.grammarNote:
**تَصحيح الأخطاء** (taṣḥīḥ al-akhṭā') = debugging; lit. 'error correction'. An iḍāfa.
**أَخطاء** = broken plural of **خَطَأ** (khaṭa') 'error'.

**إِصلاح** (iṣlāḥ) = fixing, repair. Verbal noun of أَصلَحَ 'to fix/repair'.
**أَصلَحتُ** (aṣlaḥtu) = I fixed — past tense with first-person singular suffix.

**نَشر** (nashr) = deployment (noun); also the verb **نَشَرَ** = to deploy/publish.
**الإِصدار الجَديد** = the new version — adjective follows the noun in an iḍāfa.
cards.englishPhrase: We deploy the new version today.

cards.grammarNote:
**الخادِم** (al-khādim) = the server; lit. 'the servant'. Also loanword **سيرفر** in colloquial use.
**تَعَطَّلَ** (ta'aṭṭala) = crashed/broke down — verb on تَفَعَّلَ pattern.

**قاعِدة البَيانات** (qā'idat al-bayānāt) = database; lit. 'base of data'. An iḍāfa.
**بَيانات** = data — a sound fem. plural; no single-word singular in this sense.

**تَطبيق** (taṭbīq) = application/app. Verbal noun of طَبَّقَ 'to apply/implement'.
**مَشهور** (mashhūr) = popular/famous — passive participle used as adjective.

**مَوقِع إِلِكتروني** (mawqi' iliktrūnī) = website; lit. 'electronic site'.
**أُطلِقَ** (uṭliqa) = was launched — passive past tense; root ط-ل-ق.

**وَظيفة** (waẓīfa) = function/feature; also 'a job'. From و-ظ-ف.
For a code function specifically: **دالَّة** (dālla). **لم تَكتَمِل** = not yet complete.

**ميزة** (mīza) = a feature/advantage. Fem. noun from م-ي-ز 'to distinguish'.
**مُفيدة** (mufīda) = useful — fem. active participle agreeing with ميزة.

**طَلب السَّحب** (ṭalab as-saḥb) = pull request; lit. 'pull request' — an iḍāfa. The English abbreviation 'PR' is widely used in tech.
**راجِع** (rāji') = review! — imperative of راجَعَ.
cards.phrase: مِن فَضلِك راجِع طَلب السَّحب الخاصّ بي.
cards.phraseRomanized: min faḍlika rāji' ṭalab as-saḥb al-khāṣṣ bī.

cards.grammarNote:
**اجتِماع** (ijtimā') = a meeting. Verbal noun of اجتَمَعَ 'to gather together'.
**بَعدَ الظُّهر** (ba'da aẓ-ẓuhr) = in the afternoon — temporal phrase.
cards.englishPhrase: We have a meeting this afternoon.

cards.grammarNote:
**اجتِماع يَومِيّ** (ijtimā' yawmiyy) = daily standup meeting. **يَومِيّ** = daily — nisba adjective from يَوم.
**كُلَّ صَباح** (kulla ṣabāḥ) = every morning.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a standup every morning.

cards.grammarNote:
**مَوعِد نِهائيّ** (maw'id nihā'iyy) = deadline; lit. 'final appointment'. An adjective phrase.
**يَوم الجُمعة** (yawm al-jum'a) = Friday — a definite iḍāfa.

**عَميل** ('amīl) = client, customer. Plural: **عُمَلاء** ('umalā') — broken plural.
**راضٍ** (rāḍin) = satisfied — active participle in indefinite form ends in -in.

**العَمَل مِن المَنزِل** = working from home; a common noun phrase.
Verb: **أَعمَل مِن المَنزِل** (a'mal min al-manzil) = I work from home — present tense.

**العَمَل عَن بُعد** = remote work; lit. 'work from a distance'. **عَن بُعد** = remotely.
**الفَريق** (al-farīq) = the team.

**الطَّرَفِيَّة** (aṭ-ṭarafiyya) = the terminal (command line). Also loanword **تِيرمينال**.
**افتَح** (iftaḥ) = open! — imperative of فَتَحَ.

**مُتَغَيِّر** (mutaghayyir) = variable; active participle of تَغَيَّرَ 'to change'.
**غَير مُعَرَّف** (ghayra mu'arraf) = undefined/not defined — negation with غَير.

**المُستَودَع** (al-mustawda') = repository. Noun of place from ودَعَ 'to store'; also **المَستودَع**.
Also the loanword **ريبو** (rīpō) in informal use.
cards.englishPhrase: The code is in this repository.

cards.grammarNote:
**فَرع** (far') = branch. Plural: **فُروع** (furū'). In git context also the loanword **بَرانش**.
**أَنشَأتُ** (ansha'tu) = I created — past tense from أَنشَأَ.

**مُراجَعة** (murāja'a) = review, revision. Verbal noun of راجَعَ 'to review'.
**هذا الكود** = this code; no additional particle needed before the object.

**الاختِبارات** (al-ikhtibārāt) = the tests — sound fem. plural.
**نَجَحَت** (najaḥat) = passed (fem. verb, agreeing with الاختِبارات which is fem. plural).

**تَحديث** (taḥdīth) = update. Verbal noun of حَدَّثَ/حَدَّثَ 'to update'.
**مُهِمّ** (muhimm) = important — adjective following the noun.

**خَطَأ حَرِج** (khaṭa' ḥarij) = a critical error. **حَرِج** = critical, serious.
**اكتَشَفنا** (iktashafnā) = we discovered — past tense with 1st pl. suffix.

**بيئة الإِنتاج** (bī'at al-intāj) = production environment; an iḍāfa.
**لا** (lā) + present tense jussive = prohibition: 'do not …'.

**الفَريق** (al-farīq) = the team. Plural: **الفُرَق** (al-furaq).
**رائِع** (rā'i') = great, wonderful — adjective agreeing in gender (masc.).

**مَشروع** (mashrū') = project. Passive participle of شَرَعَ used as a noun.
**مُثير للاهتِمام** (muthīr lil-ihtimām) = interesting — active participle + preposition phrase.

**إِطلاق** (iṭlāq) = launch/release. Verbal noun of أَطلَقَ 'to launch'.
**الأُسبوع القادِم** (al-usbū' al-qādim) = next week.
cards.englishPhrase: We launch the product next week.

cards.grammarNote:
**إِصدار** (iṣdār) = version, release. Verbal noun of أَصدَرَ 'to issue/release'.
**الأَحدَث** (al-aḥdath) = the latest — elative adjective (superlative form).

**إِعداد** (i'dād) = configuration/setup. Verbal noun of أَعَدَّ 'to prepare'.
Verb: **أُعِدّ** (u'idd) = I configure/set up.
cards.englishPhrase: I need to configure the server.

cards.grammarNote:
**بيئة** (bī'a) = environment. Fem. noun; plural: **بيئات** (bī'āt).
**مُختَلِفة** (mukhtalifa) = different — fem. active participle as adjective.
cards.englishPhrase: The dev and prod environments are different.

cards.grammarNote:
**تَشغيل** (tashghīl) = running/execution. Verbal noun of شَغَّلَ 'to run/operate'.
Imperative: **شَغِّل** (shaghghil) = run!

**سِجِلّ** (sijill) = log, record. Plural: **سِجِلّات** (sijillāt).
**تَحَقَّق مِن** (taḥaqqaq min) = check/verify — imperative of تَحَقَّقَ.

**رَفَعَ** (rafa'a) = to push/upload (code). **رَفَعتُ** = I pushed.
In git context the English 'push' is also used: **دَفَعتُ** (dafa'tu) 'I pushed'.
cards.englishPhrase: I pushed the code to the repository.

cards.grammarNote:
**تَكامُل** (takāmul) = integration. Verbal noun of تَكامَلَ 'to integrate/be complementary'.
**فَشِلَ** (fashila) = failed — root ف-ش-ل.

**تَعليق** (ta'līq) = comment (in code or general). Verbal noun of عَلَّقَ 'to comment'.
Plural: **تَعليقات** (ta'līqāt).

**يَحتاج** (yaḥtāj) = he/it needs; root ح-و-ج on اِفتَعَلَ pattern.
**أَحتاج إلى** (aḥtāj ilā) = I need — the preposition إلى is required after this verb.

**أَكمَلَ** (akmala) = to complete, finish. Root ك-م-ل on أَفعَلَ pattern.
Also: **انتَهى** (intahā) = finished/ended. **أَكمَلتُ** = I completed.
al-hātif adh-dhakiyy
cards.englishPhrase:
**الهاتف الذكيّ** (al-hātif adh-dhakiyy) = 'the intelligent phone'.
**الجوّال / الموبايل** (al-jawwāl / al-mōbāyl) = mobile phone (colloquial).

cards.grammarNote: al-ḥāsūb al-maḥmūl
cards.englishPhrase:
**الحاسوب المحمول** (al-ḥāsūb al-maḥmūl) = 'the carried computer'.
**اللابتوب** (al-lābtōb) = laptop (loanword, common).

cards.grammarNote: al-ḥāsūb
ash-shāsha
lawḥat al-mafātīḥ
cards.englishPhrase:
**لوحة المفاتيح** (lawḥat al-mafātīḥ) = 'board of the keys'.
**مِفتاح** (miftāḥ) = a key (plural مفاتيح).

cards.grammarNote: ash-shāḥin
cards.englishPhrase:
**الشاحن** (ash-shāḥin) = charger, from **شحن** 'to charge'.
 The *fāʿil* active-participle pattern names the device that does the action.

cards.grammarNote: al-baṭṭāriyya
al-wāy fāy
cards.englishPhrase:
**الواي فاي** (al-wāy fāy) = wifi (loanword).
**الشبكة اللاسلكية** (ash-shabaka al-lā-silkiyya) = wireless network (formal).
cards.phraseRomanized: mā hiya kalimat sirr al-wāy fāy?
cards.literal: ما هي كَلِمة سِرّ الواي فاي؟

cards.grammarNote: al-intarnit
cards.phrase: There's no internet in the house.

cards.grammarNote: at-taṭbīq
cards.englishPhrase:
**التطبيق** (at-taṭbīq) = application (plural **تطبيقات** taṭbīqāt).
 From the root **ط-ب-ق** 'to apply'.

cards.grammarNote: ḥammala / yuḥammil
cards.englishPhrase:
**حَمّلَ** (ḥammala) = to download (Form II of *ḥamala* 'to carry').
**رَفَعَ** (rafaʿa) = to upload.
cards.phrase: I want to download the file.

cards.grammarNote: thabbata / yuthabbit
cards.englishPhrase:
**ثَبَّتَ** (thabbata) = to install / fix in place (Form II).
**حَذَفَ** (ḥadhafa) = to delete / uninstall.

cards.grammarNote: kalimat as-sirr
cards.englishPhrase:
**كلمة السرّ** (kalimat as-sirr) = 'word of the secret'.
 Also **كلمة المرور** (kalimat al-murūr).

cards.grammarNote: as-sammāʿāt
al-kāmīrā
cards.englishPhrase:
**الكاميرا** (al-kāmīrā) = camera (feminine, loanword).
**آلة التصوير** (ālat at-taṣwīr) = camera (native term).

cards.grammarNote: aṣ-ṣūra
cards.englishPhrase:
**الصورة** (aṣ-ṣūra) = photo / picture (plural **صُوَر** ṣuwar).
**اِلتَقَطَ صورة** (iltaqaṭa ṣūra) = to take a photo.
cards.phrase: Can you take a photo of us?
cards.phraseRomanized: hal yumkinuka an taltaqiṭ lanā ṣūra?
cards.literal: هل يُمكِنُك أَن تَلتَقِط لنا صورة؟

cards.grammarNote: shaḥana / yashḥan
cards.englishPhrase:
**شَحَنَ** (shaḥana) = to charge (a device); root **ش-ح-ن**.
**الشاحن** (ash-shāḥin) = the charger (see above).
cards.phrase: I need to charge the phone.

cards.grammarNote: ar-risāla
cards.phrase: I'll send you a message later.

cards.grammarNote: al-barīd al-iliktrūnī
cards.englishPhrase:
**البريد الإلكتروني** (al-barīd al-iliktrūnī) = 'the electronic mail'.
**الإيميل** (al-īmayl) = email (loanword, colloquial).
cards.phrase: I'll send you an email tomorrow.

cards.grammarNote: shaghghala / yushaghghil
cards.englishPhrase:
**شَغّلَ** (shaghghala) = to turn on / operate (Form II).
**فَتَحَ** (fataḥa) 'to open' is also used for switching things on.

cards.grammarNote: aṭfaʾa / yuṭfiʾ
cards.englishPhrase:
**أَطفَأَ** (aṭfaʾa) = to turn off / extinguish (Form IV).
 Opposite of **شَغّلَ**.

cards.grammarNote: al-ishʿār
cards.englishPhrase:
**الإشعار** (al-ishʿār) = notification (plural **إشعارات** ishʿārāt).
 From the root **ش-ع-ر** 'to be aware'.

cards.grammarNote: ḥaddatha / yuḥaddith
cards.englishPhrase:
**حَدَّثَ** (ḥaddatha) = to update (Form II, from *ḥadīth* 'new / recent').
**التحديث** (at-taḥdīth) = the update (noun).

cards.grammarNote: al-bathth al-mubāshir
cards.englishPhrase:
**البث المباشر** (al-bathth al-mubāshir) = 'direct broadcasting', i.e. live streaming.
**بَثَّ** (baththa) = to broadcast / stream.

cards.grammarNote:
**زِنزانة** (zinzāna) = dungeon, prison cell. Fem. noun; plural: **زَنازين** (zanāzīn) — broken plural.
**مُظلِمة** (muẓlima) = dark — fem. adjective agreeing with زِنزانة.

**تِنِّين** (tinnīn) = dragon. In Arabic tradition a powerful sea/sky serpent. Plural: **تَنانين** (tanānīn).
**يَحرُس** (yaḥrus) = guards — present tense from ح-ر-س.
cards.englishPhrase: A huge dragon guards the treasure.

cards.grammarNote:
**مُهِمَّة** (muhimma) = mission/quest. Fem. noun; plural: **مَهامّ** (mahāmm) — broken plural.
**قَبِلنا** (qabilnā) = we accepted — past tense.

**مُغامَرة** (mughāmara) = adventure. Verbal noun of غامَرَ 'to venture/risk'.
**خَطيرة** (khaṭīra) = dangerous — fem. adjective agreeing with مُغامَرة.

**حَملة** (ḥamla) = campaign (a series of linked sessions). Fem. noun from ح-م-ل.
**اِستَمَرَّت** (istamarrat) = lasted — fem. past tense agreeing with حَملة.

**شَخصِيَّة** (shakhṣiyya) = character/personality. Fem. noun; plural: **شَخصِيّات** (shakhṣiyyāt).
**أَنشَأتُ** (ansha'tu) = I created — past tense from أَنشَأَ.

**ساحِر** (sāḥir) = wizard, sorcerer. Active participle of سَحَرَ 'to cast magic'.
**أَطلَقَ** (aṭlaqa) = cast/launched — past tense from ط-ل-ق.

**مُحارِب** (muḥārib) = warrior. Active participle of حارَبَ 'to fight/war against'.
**رَفَعَ** (rafa'a) = raised — past tense from ر-ف-ع.

**لِصّ** (liṣṣ) = thief, rogue. Plural: **لُصوص** (luṣūṣ).
**سَرَقَ** (saraqa) = stole — past tense from س-ر-ق.

**فارِس مُقَدَّس** (fāris muqaddas) = paladin; lit. 'holy knight'. **فارِس** = knight/horseman.
**شُجاع** (shujā') = brave — adjective following the noun.

**مُتَجَوِّل** (mutajawwil) = ranger/wanderer. Active participle of تَجَوَّلَ 'to roam'.
**بارِع في** (bāri' fī) = skilled at — iḍāfa + في + noun.
cards.englishPhrase: The ranger is skilled at archery.

cards.grammarNote:
**سَيِّد الزَّنازين** (sayyid az-zanāzīn) = dungeon master; lit. 'lord of the dungeons'. An iḍāfa.
Also called **الراوي** (ar-rāwī) 'the narrator' in Arabic D&D communities.
cards.englishPhrase: The dungeon master described the scene.

cards.grammarNote:
**تَعويذة** (ta'wīdha) = spell, charm. From عَوَّذَ 'to protect by magic'. Plural: **تَعاويذ** (ta'āwīdh).
**قَوِيَّة** (qawiyya) = powerful — fem. adjective agreeing with تَعويذة.

**طِلسم** (ṭilsam) = incantation, talisman. Plural: **طَلاسِم** (ṭalāsim).
**رَدَّدَت** (raddadat) = she recited — intensive verb form with fem. subject.

**سِحر** (siḥr) = magic. Root س-ح-ر. The Quran mentions سِحر making it a well-known classical word.
**مَمتلِئة بـ** (mumtali'a bi-) = full of — fem. participle + prep.
cards.englishPhrase: The forest is full of magic.

cards.grammarNote:
**جُرعة سِحرِيَّة** (jur'a siḥriyya) = a magic potion; lit. 'magical sip/dose'.
**اِشرَب** (ishrab) = drink! — imperative of شَرِبَ.

**سَيف** (sayf) = sword. Plural: **سُيوف** (suyūf) — broken plural.
**حادّ** (ḥādd) = sharp — adjective following the definite noun.

**دِرع** (dir') = shield/armor. Fem. or masc. depending on dialect; classical Arabic treats it as fem.
**اِحجُب** (iḥjub) = block! — imperative of حَجَبَ.
cards.englishPhrase: Block the attack with your shield.

cards.grammarNote:
**دِرع** (dir') can mean both shield and body armor in classical Arabic. For body armor also **دِرع كاملة** or **بَدَلة حِماية**.
**اِلبَس** (ilbas) = put on! — imperative of لَبِسَ 'to wear'.

**نَرد** (nard) = dice. From Persian نَرد; the game of backgammon is also called نَرد in Arabic.
Singular die: **حَجَر النَّرد** (ḥajar an-nard).
cards.englishPhrase: There are some dice on the table.

cards.grammarNote:
**رَمي النَّرد** (ramī an-nard) = rolling the dice. An iḍāfa; **رَمي** is the verbal noun of رَمى 'to throw'.
**دَورُك** (dawruka) = your turn.
cards.englishPhrase: It's your turn to roll the dice.

cards.grammarNote:
**ضَربة حاسِمة** (ḍarba ḥāsima) = critical hit; lit. 'decisive blow'. **حاسِمة** = decisive — fem. active participle.
**كانَت** (kānat) = was (fem.) — past tense copula.

**الارتِقاء بالمُستوى** = leveling up. **ارتَقى** (irtaqā) = to rise in level/rank.
**ارتَقَت شَخصِيَّتي** = my character leveled up — fem. verb agreeing with شَخصِيَّة.

**نِقاط الخِبرة** (niqāṭ al-khibra) = experience points (XP). An iḍāfa.
**حَصَلتَ على** (ḥaṣalta 'alā) = you gained — past tense + preposition على.
cards.englishPhrase: You gained a lot of experience points.
cards.phrase: حَصَلتَ على الكَثير مِن نِقاط الخِبرة.

cards.grammarNote:
**وَحش** (waḥsh) = monster, beast. Plural: **وُحوش** (wuḥūsh).
**ظَهَرَ** (ẓahara) = appeared — past tense from ظ-ه-ر.

**جِنِّيّ صَغير** (jinniyy ṣaghīr) = goblin; lit. 'small jinn'. The jinn is the closest Arabic cultural equivalent.
Also the loanword **جوبلن** (goblin) in modern Arabic fantasy.

**كَنز** (kanz) = treasure, hoard. Plural: **كُنوز** (kunūz).
**وَجَدنا** (wajadnā) = we found — past tense from و-ج-د.

**خَريطة** (kharīṭa) = map. Fem. noun; plural: **خَرائِط** (kharā'iṭ).
**اُنظُر إلى** (unẓur ilā) = look at — imperative + preposition.

**حانة** (ḥāna) = tavern. Fem. noun from ح-ن-و.
**نَستَريح** (nastarīḥ) = we rest — present tense from اِستَراحَ 'to rest'.

**فِرقة المُغامِرين** (firqat al-mughāmirīn) = adventuring party; an iḍāfa.
**مُغامِرين** = masc. sound plural of **مُغامِر** (mughāmir) 'adventurer'.

**مَسحور** (masḥūr) = enchanted, bewitched. Passive participle of سَحَرَ 'to bewitch/enchant'.
**هذا السَّيف** = this sword — definite masc. pointing phrase.

**هُجوم** (hujūm) = attack (noun). Verb: **هاجَمَ** (hājama) = to attack.
**هاجِم** (hājim) = attack! — imperative of هاجَمَ.

**هَرَبَ** (haraba) = he fled. Root ه-ر-ب. **هَرَبوا** = they fled.
**قَرَّروا** (qarrарū) = they decided — past tense of قَرَّرَ.

**شَفى** (shafā) = to heal, cure. Root ش-ف-ي. **شَفاءً** = healing (noun).
**كاهِن** (kāhin) = cleric/priest; **عَالَجَ** (ʿālaja) = treated/healed — fā'ala pattern.

**دِفاع** (difā') = defense (noun). Verb: **دافَعَ** (dāfa'a) = to defend.
**يَجِب عَلَينا** (yajibu 'alaynā) = we must — present tense obligation.

**اِستِكشاف** (istikshāf) = exploration. Verbal noun of اِستَكشَفَ 'to explore/discover'.
**لِنَستَكشِف** (li-nastakshif) = let's explore — jussive with لِـ prefix.

**نِقاط الصِّحَّة** (niqāṭ aṣ-ṣiḥḥa) = hit points/HP; lit. 'health points'. An iḍāfa.
**مُنخَفِضة** (munkhafiḍa) = low — fem. active participle agreeing with نِقاط (fem. pl.).

**دَور** (dawr) = turn, round. Plural: **أَدوار** (adwār).
**دَوري الآن** (dawrī al-ān) = it's my turn now — possessive suffix ـي on دَور.

**نَصر** (naṣr) = victory. Root ن-ص-ر. **اِنتَصَرنا** (intaṣarnā) = we triumphed.
**في النِّهاية** (fī an-nihāya) = in the end — idiomatic phrase.
cards.englishPhrase: In the end we achieved victory.

cards.grammarNote:
**عَدوّ** ('aduww) = enemy. Plural: **أَعداء** ('a'dā') — broken plural.
**يَقتَرِب** (yaqtarib) = getting closer — present tense from اِقتَرَبَ.

**فَخّ** (fakhkh) = trap. Plural: **فِخاخ** (fikhākh).
**اِحذَر** (iḥdhar) = watch out! — imperative of حَذِرَ. Followed by مِن = 'watch out for'.

**غَنيمة** (ghanīma) = loot, spoils. Plural: **غَنائِم** (ghanā'im) — broken plural.
**قَسَّمنا** (qassamnā) = we split — past tense from قَسَّمَ 'to divide'.

**صاحِب الفُندُق** (ṣāḥib al-funduq) = innkeeper; lit. 'owner of the inn'. An iḍāfa.
**أَخبَرَنا** (akhbaranā) = told us — past tense of أَخبَرَ 'to inform'.
cards.englishPhrase: The innkeeper gave us some news.

cards.grammarNote:
**قَوس** (qaws) = bow (weapon). Plural: **أَقواس** (aqwās). Arrow: **سَهم** (sahm).
**أَصابَت** (aṣābat) = hit/struck (fem.) — fem. verb agreeing with fem. subject هي.
cards.englishPhrase: She hit the target with her bow.

cards.grammarNote:
**جَلسة لَعِب** (jalsat la'ib) = a game session. An iḍāfa.
**الجَلسة** (al-jalsa) = the session; **اللَّيلة** (al-layla) = tonight.

**قاعِدة** (qā'ida) = rule. Plural: **قَواعِد** (qawā'id) — broken plural.
**اِلتَزِم بـ** (iltazim bi-) = follow/comply with — imperative of اِلتَزَمَ.

**المُبادَأة** (al-mubāda'a) = initiative, the right to go first. Verbal noun of بادَأَ 'to initiate'.
**تَرتيب** (tartīb) = order/sequence — verbal noun of رَتَّبَ.

**نَرد العِشرين وَجهًا** = the twenty-sided die. An iḍāfa + number phrase.
**اِستَخدِم** (istakhdim) = use! — imperative of اِستَخدَمَ 'to use'.
cards.englishPhrase: Use the d20 for the check.

cards.grammarNote:
**عيد الفِطر** ('Īd al-Fiṭr) = the festival marking the end of Ramadan. **عيد** = festival; **الفِطر** = the breaking (of fast). An iḍāfa.
**أَهمّ** (ahamm) = most important — elative (superlative) adjective.
cards.englishPhrase: Eid al-Fitr is one of the most important holidays.
cards.phrase: عيد الفِطر مِن أَهمّ الأَعياد الإِسلامِيَّة.
literal: is one of the most important

cards.grammarNote:
**عيد الأَضحى** ('Īd al-Aḍḥā) = the Festival of Sacrifice, commemorating Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son. **الأَضحى** = the sacrifice.
**يُضَحّى فيه** = 'sacrifice is made during it' — passive present tense.
cards.englishPhrase: On Eid al-Adha families sacrifice an animal.
cards.phrase: في عيد الأَضحى تُضَحّي العائِلات بِحَيَوان.

cards.grammarNote:
**رَمَضان** (Ramaḍān) = the holy month of fasting. From **رَمَض** 'burning heat'.
**يَصوم** (yaṣūm) = fasts — present tense from صامَ (ṣāma) 'to fast'.

**إِفطار** (ifṭār) = breaking the fast; the evening meal in Ramadan. Verbal noun of أَفطَرَ 'to break one's fast'.
**بعدَ غُروب الشَّمس** = after sunset — temporal phrase.
cards.englishPhrase: Iftar is the meal after sunset.
cards.phrase: الإِفطار وَجبة ما بَعدَ غُروب الشَّمس.
cards.phraseRomanized: al-ifṭār wajbat mā ba'da ghurūb ash-shams.

cards.grammarNote:
**قَهوة عَرَبِيَّة** (qahwa 'arabiyya) = Arabic coffee, often flavored with cardamom. **قَهوة** (qahwa) = coffee — a fem. noun.
**يُقَدِّمون** (yuqaddimūn) = they serve — present tense from قَدَّمَ 'to present'.
cards.englishPhrase: Arabic coffee is served as a sign of hospitality.

cards.grammarNote:
**شاي بالنَّعناع** (shāy bin-na'nā') = mint tea. **شاي** = tea; **النَّعناع** = mint.
In Moroccan Arabic culture, **أتاي** (atāy) is the traditional poured tea ceremony.
cards.englishPhrase: Moroccan mint tea is a symbol of friendship.

cards.grammarNote:
**كَرَم الضِّيافة** (karam aḍ-ḍiyāfa) = hospitality; lit. 'generosity of hosting'. An iḍāfa.
**كَرَم** = generosity — a core Arab virtue; **ضِيافة** = hosting/reception.
cards.englishPhrase: Hospitality is an important Arab value.

cards.grammarNote:
**الخَطّ العَرَبيّ** (al-khaṭṭ al-'arabiyy) = Arabic calligraphy. **خَطّ** = script/line/style of writing.
Six classical scripts: نَسخ، رُقعة، ثُلُث، دِيواني، كوفي، فارِسي.
cards.englishPhrase: Arabic calligraphy is a revered art form.

cards.grammarNote:
**القُرآن الكَريم** (al-Qur'ān al-Karīm) = the Noble Quran. **القُرآن** = the Quran; **الكَريم** = noble/generous — an adjective.
**يَتلو** (yatlū) = recites — present tense from تَلا.
cards.englishPhrase: The Quran is recited during Ramadan.

cards.grammarNote:
**مَسجِد** (masjid) = mosque. Noun of place from س-ج-د 'to prostrate'. Plural: **مَساجِد** (masājid).
**جامِع** (jāmi') specifically means a Friday/congregational mosque.
cards.englishPhrase: The mosque is the center of community life.

cards.grammarNote:
**الأَذان** (al-adhān) = the call to prayer, recited five times daily. From أَذِنَ 'to give permission/notice'.
**المُؤَذِّن** (al-mu'adhdhin) = the muezzin, the one who calls.
cards.englishPhrase: The call to prayer is heard five times a day.
cards.phrase: يُرَدَّد الأَذان خَمسَ مَرّات في اليَوم.
cards.phraseRomanized: yuraddad al-adhān khamsa marrāt fī al-yawm.

cards.grammarNote:
**عائِلة** ('ā'ila) = family. Also **أُسرة** (usra). Plural: **عائِلات** / **أُسَر**.
**العائِلة** is a cornerstone of Arab social life; extended family meals are central to culture.
cards.englishPhrase: Family is very important in Arab culture.
cards.phrase: العائِلة مُهِمَّة جِدًّا في الثَّقافة العَرَبِيَّة.
cards.phraseRomanized: al-'ā'ila muhimma jiddan fī ath-thaqāfa al-'arabiyya.

cards.grammarNote:
**سوق** (sūq) = market, souk. Masc. or fem. depending on dialect. Plural: **أَسواق** (aswāq).
**مُزدَحِم** (muzdaḥim) = crowded — passive participle used as adjective.
cards.englishPhrase: The souk is full of colors and smells.

cards.grammarNote:
**تَمر** (tamr) = dates (dried). A collective noun; one date: **تَمرة** (tamra).
**بالتَّمر** (bit-tamr) = with dates; traditional to break the Ramadan fast with a date.
cards.englishPhrase: Dates are eaten to break the fast.

cards.grammarNote:
**حِنَّاء** (ḥinnā') = henna. A fem. noun; the plant and the reddish dye used in celebrations.
**تُزَيِّن** (tuzayyin) = decorates — present tense of زَيَّنَ 'to adorn'.
cards.englishPhrase: Henna is used to decorate hands at weddings.
cards.phrase: تُستَخدَم الحِنَّاء لتَزيين الأَيدي في الأَعراس.
cards.phraseRomanized: tustakhdamu al-ḥinnā' li-tazīyīn al-aydī fī al-a'rās.

cards.grammarNote:
**جَمَل** (jamal) = camel (male). Female camel: **ناقة** (nāqa). Plural: **جِمال** (jimāl).
**سَفينة الصَّحراء** (safīnat aṣ-ṣaḥrā') = 'ship of the desert' — a famous Arabic metaphor.
cards.englishPhrase: The camel is called the ship of the desert.

cards.grammarNote:
**مَقام** (maqām) = a musical mode/scale in Arabic music. Plural: **مَقامات** (maqāmāt).
Each مَقام carries a distinct mood; **مَقام الرَّست** is a common opening maqam.
cards.englishPhrase: Arabic music is based on maqamat.

cards.grammarNote:
**عود** ('ūd) = the oud, ancestor of the European lute. From **عود** 'wood'.
**يَعزِف على** (ya'zif 'alā) = plays (an instrument) — verb + على.

**حَمّام** (ḥammām) = public bathhouse, a social and cleansing institution across the Arab world.
**ثَقافيّ** (thaqāfiyy) = cultural — nisba adjective from ثَقافة.
cards.englishPhrase: The hammam is a cultural tradition.

cards.grammarNote:
**الأَرقام العَرَبِيَّة** (al-arqām al-'arabiyya) = Arabic numerals, which gave the world the modern number system.
**الأَرقام الهِندِيَّة** is the term used in Arab countries for the Eastern Arabic numerals (٠١٢٣…).
cards.englishPhrase: Arabic numerals are used around the world.
cards.phrase: تُستَخدَم الأَرقام العَرَبِيَّة في أَنحاء العالَم.
cards.phraseRomanized: tustakhdamu al-arqām al-'arabiyya fī anḥā' al-'ālam.

cards.grammarNote:
**أَلف لَيلة ولَيلة** (Alf Layla wa-Layla) = One Thousand and One Nights. A compound noun phrase.
**أَلف** = one thousand; the title uses a rhyming repetition (لَيلة … ولَيلة) typical of Arabic literary style.
cards.englishPhrase: One Thousand and One Nights is a famous Arabic literary work.
cards.phrase: أَلف لَيلة ولَيلة مِن أَشهَر الأَعمال الأَدَبِيَّة العَرَبِيَّة.
cards.phraseRomanized: Alf Layla wa-Layla min ashhār al-a'māl al-adabiyya al-'arabiyya.
literal: is one of the most famous

cards.grammarNote:
**قَبيلة** (qabīla) = tribe, clan. Plural: **قَبائِل** (qabā'il). **الانتِماء القَبَلي** = tribal belonging.
Tribal identity remains socially important in many Arab regions.
cards.englishPhrase: Tribal bonds are strong in many Arab communities.
cards.phrase: الرَّوابِط القَبَلِيَّة قَوِيَّة في كَثير مِن المُجتَمَعات العَرَبِيَّة.
cards.phraseRomanized: ar-rawābiṭ al-qabaliyya qawiyya fī kathīr min al-mujtama'āt al-'arabiyya.

cards.grammarNote:
**مَثَل** (mathal) = proverb, saying. Plural: **أَمثال** (amthāl). **ضَرَبَ المَثَل** = to give an example.
Arabic is rich in proverbs; e.g. **الصَّبر مِفتاح الفَرَج** 'patience is the key to relief'.
cards.englishPhrase: Arab culture is rich in proverbs.

cards.grammarNote:
**بَقلاوة** (baqlāwa) = baklava, a sweet pastry of layered filo, nuts, and syrup. From Turkish/Arabic.
Fem. noun; **حُلوى** (ḥulwā) = sweets/candy in general.
cards.englishPhrase: Baklava is a popular sweet in the Arab world.
cards.phrase: البَقلاوة حَلوى مَشهورة في العالَم العَرَبيّ.
cards.phraseRomanized: al-baqlāwa ḥalwā mashhūra fī al-'ālam al-'arabiyy.

cards.grammarNote:
**مَنسَف** (mansaf) = mansaf, Jordan's national dish: lamb on rice with fermented dried yogurt (جَميد).
**الطَّبَق الوَطَنيّ** (aṭ-ṭabaq al-waṭaniyy) = the national dish.

**صَحراء** (ṣaḥrā') = desert. Fem. noun; includes the famous الصَّحراء الكُبرى (the Sahara).
**شاسِعة** (shāsi'a) = vast — fem. active participle.
cards.englishPhrase: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
cards.phrase: الصَّحراء الكُبرى أَكبَر صَحراء حارَّة في العالَم.
cards.phraseRomanized: aṣ-Ṣaḥrā' al-Kubrā akbar ṣaḥrā' ḥārra fī al-'ālam.

cards.grammarNote:
**كَرَم** (karam) = generosity. A core Arab virtue and one of the highest compliments.
**كَريم** (karīm) = generous — adjective; divine name: **الكَريم** (God the Generous).
cards.englishPhrase: Generosity is a hallmark of Arab character.
cards.phrase: الكَرَم صِفة أَصيلة في الشَّخصِيَّة العَرَبِيَّة.
cards.phraseRomanized: al-karam ṣifa aṣīla fī ash-shakhṣiyya al-'arabiyya.
